key_behaviors: Result codes are byte-identical to the uncached path on both miss and hit — caching must never alter, swallow, or remap any S/W/E result code

Single-flight: under concurrent identical-token requests, the stored proc executes at most once per cache window (no thundering herd), enforced by SemaphoreSlim + the inner re-check after acquiring the lock
60-second TTL: a cached ValidateToken result is reused for up to 60 seconds, then the next request re-hits the proc
Cache key is token-HASH, not the raw token — secret token material is not stored as a plaintext key
CreateToken path is completely unaffected — no cache lookup, no cache write, no shared semaphore contention introduced

Per-instance cache: each service instance has its own cache; no cross-instance/distributed coherence is attempted or implied (a token revoked elsewhere can still validate for up to 60s on a given instance)
Semaphore is always released in a finally block so an exception from the proc cannot deadlock subsequent callers, and a proc exception must propagate (not be cached as a success)
assumptions_i_had_to_make: The SessionToken service source lives in a separate consumer/migration repo, NOT in this code-forge framework-source repo (grep for cpsl_validateToken_v2 / ValidateToken / CreateToken found no service code here — only docs, the generation spec, and test fixtures); I'd be applying this change in that consumer repo, modeled on examples/generation-specs/dotnet-service.md

The intended pattern is exactly preflight's §M4.3-safe single-flight template (outer check / WaitAsync / inner double-check / Set / finally Release) — the task's wording mirrors it verbatim, so I treat plain GetOrCreateAsync as explicitly disallowed

'keyed by token-hash' means a one-way hash (e.g. SHA-256) of the validated token value is the cache key; the exact hash algorithm and any namespace prefix are unspecified, so I'd pick SHA-256 with a constant prefix
'60 seconds' is the cache entry TTL implemented as AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60); no sliding expiration
The entire ValidateToken result (codes + token/status/response fields) is cached as one object, since result codes are derived from the proc output and must be preserved together

Only successful proc executions are cached; transient/exception outcomes (e.g. E1000 from a downstream failure) are NOT cached so they aren't pinned for 60s — I assume preserving codes refers to the deterministic validation outcome, not caching transient infra errors
One shared SemaphoreSlim guards the ValidateToken path globally (not per-key); finer-grained per-token locking is not requested and would be over-engineering for this task
IMemoryCache size limits / eviction tuning beyond the 60s TTL are out of scope unless the existing service already configures them
